subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should this issue be fixed as a narrow stale OpenAI route/hot-reload repair now, folded into the broader session model/auth state resolver, or treated as expected behavior when the session was explicitly switched to OpenAI?
rationale: Source inspection proves a correctly selected DeepSeek route should not be claimed directly by Codex, but the live report mixes Codex hot reload, persisted selected/runtime model state, and an explicit `/model openai` clarification, so automation should not choose the permanent session-state contract.

options.title: Fix narrow route drift first
options.body: Repair stale or auto-created OpenAI session pins and Codex hot-reload drift while keeping the broader resolver tracker open for cleanup.

options.title: Fold into resolver tracker
options.body: Move this DeepSeek/Codex hot-reload scenario into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87957 acceptance criteria and resolve it with the shared selected/runtime/auth-state resolver.

options.title: Treat explicit OpenAI as expected
options.body: If maintainers decide the behavior follows the reporter's manual `/model openai` switch, keep OpenAI-through-Codex behavior and improve status or doctor diagnostics instead.

recommendation.title: Fix narrow route drift first
recommendation.body: Repair stale or auto-created OpenAI session pins and Codex hot-reload drift while keeping the broader resolver tracker open for cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across OpenAI provider identity, Codex harness policy, and the session/status paths involved in the decision.
